title: Tenali Raman Tale 143

full_text:
A wealthy merchant of Vijayanagara named Somadatta was murdered and robbed of five hundred gold coins in an alley behind the Great Shiva Temple.
A notorious rogue named Shankara was arrested as the primary suspect, having been seen near the temple.
However, Shankara produced a sworn witness, an astrologer named Keshava, who swore an oath before the court:
'Shankara is innocent! At the exact hour of the murder—precisely two hours after sunrise on Friday morning—Shankara was sitting with me on the eastern steps of the temple, resting in the cool shadow of the temple spire, studying his horoscope!'

Because the alibi was supported by a respected astrologer, the court was on the verge of releasing Shankara.
Tenali Raman stepped forward:
'Maharaj, let us examine the astrologer’s astronomical testimony.'

Tenali turned to Keshava:
'Revered Astrologer, you swear that you and Shankara were resting in the shadow of the great temple spire on the **eastern steps** two hours after sunrise?'
Keshava puffed out his chest: 'I swear it upon the sacred scriptures! The shadow was cool and dark upon our heads!'

Tenali Raman burst into laughter:
'Maharaj! The alibi is a fabricated, perjured lie!'
The King demanded: 'How dost thou know, Tenali?'

Tenali explained the basic laws of solar geometry:
'The sun rises in the **East**!
Two hours after sunrise, the morning sun is climbing high in the eastern sky!
Therefore, the shadow of any building, pillar, or temple spire falls toward the **WEST**!
The eastern steps of the temple were bathed in blazing, direct morning sunlight!
The shadow of the temple spire could not possibly fall upon the eastern steps; it fell upon the western garden!
Only a liar who was never there would claim to sit in a western shadow on an eastern staircase!'

The astrologer’s knees buckled in terror. He confessed that Shankara had bribed him with fifty gold coins to fabricate the alibi.
Shankara broke down, confessed the murder, and led the guards to the stolen gold.
King Krishnadevaraya embraced Tenali Raman:
'Tenali, while lawyers argue words, thou dost call upon the sun itself to testify to the truth!'
Justice was delivered, and Tenali’s astronomical deduction was hailed throughout the empire.
moral: A liar who invents a false alibi is trapped by the immutable physics of the sun.
